question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

He gnashed his teeth at his son's actions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. expressed rage.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to gnash one's teeth" means to grind or clench the teeth together, usually as a sign of great anger, rage or frustration. (क्रोध से दाँत पीसना)

◦ Example: He gnashed his teeth in fury when he heard the unfair verdict.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "disappointment", Option 3 "sadness" and Option 4 "joy" do not capture the sense of intense anger conveyed by the idiom.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of anger: "to see red", "to fly off the handle", "to blow one's top", "to be up in arms".

question:
Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The concert was canceeled due to rain.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Cancelled.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Cancelled", the past tense of "cancel", meaning called off or stopped (an event/plan). (रद्द किया गया)

◦ Example: The match was cancelled because of heavy rain.

• Spelling key: CAN + CEL + LED — in British English the "l" is doubled (cancelled); note "cancel" has only one "l" but "cancelled/cancelling" double it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 4 ("Cancealed", "Cancaeled", "Cencelled") are all misspellings.

NOTE

• Related forms: cancel, cancelled/cancelling (British), cancellation (always double "l"). American spelling "canceled" uses a single "l", but "cancellation" always keeps the double "l".

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Run errands
option_1: To go out to buy or do something
option_2: To participate in a race through unfair means
option_3: To finish running before the end point
option_4: To do something incorrectly or erroneous in haste
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To go out to buy or do something.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to run errands" means to make short trips to perform small tasks or duties, such as going out to buy things, deliver messages or complete odd jobs. (छोटे-मोटे काम निपटाना)

◦ Example: She spent the morning running errands — buying groceries and posting letters.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2, 3 and 4 relate literally to "running" or doing something wrongly, and miss the idiomatic meaning.

NOTE

• An "errand" is a short journey to complete a small task. "Run errands", "an errand boy" and "a fool's errand" (a pointless task) are common expressions.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

He cheated in the [A] / examination, making his [B] / already-falling academic [C] / credentials worst. [D]
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. D (credentials worst).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The comparative degree "worse" is required, not the superlative "worst". His action made his credentials worse (comparing the new state with the earlier one), not "worst".

◦ Correct: ... making his already-falling academic credentials worse.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 (segment D).

Additional Information

• Segments A, B and C are grammatically correct.

NOTE

• Irregular comparison: bad – worse – worst. Use the comparative "worse" when comparing two states/things; use the superlative "worst" (with "the") for the lowest of three or more.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Conscious
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Unaware.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Conscious" means aware of and responding to one's surroundings; awake and knowing. Its antonym is "unaware", meaning not knowing or not perceiving something. (सचेत का विलोम — अनजान)

◦ Example: She was conscious of the danger, but he was completely unaware of it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Secure" (safe), Option 3 "Sensible" (practical) and Option 4 "Sentimental" (emotional) are unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of conscious: aware, awake, alert, mindful.

• Antonyms: unaware, unconscious, oblivious, ignorant.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

Our _____ conducted a _____ to get everyone's opinion.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. principal; poll.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Principal" (a noun) means the head of a school/college, while "poll" means a survey of opinion / voting. The sentence needs the head of the institution conducting an opinion survey.

◦ Correct: Our principal conducted a poll to get everyone's opinion.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Principle" (a noun) means a rule or moral belief — wrong here.

• "Pole" means a long rod or a geographic/magnetic point — wrong here.

NOTE

• Confusable pairs: Principal (head / main) vs Principle (a rule/belief); Poll (a survey/vote) vs Pole (a rod / the ends of the Earth's axis). "The principal is my pal" is a common memory trick.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

He is waiting / at airport to receive / Mr. Smith, who is / coming from South Africa.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. at airport to receive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The noun "airport" is a specific, particular place here and needs the definite article "the" — "at the airport".

◦ Correct: He is waiting at the airport to receive Mr. Smith, who is coming from South Africa.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "He is waiting", "Mr. Smith, who is" and "coming from South Africa" are all correct.

NOTE

• Use "the" before singular countable nouns referring to a specific thing (the airport, the station, the office). We say "go to the airport", "at the station", but a few fixed phrases drop "the" (go to school, go to bed, at home).

question:
Select the most appropriate degree of comparison to fill in the blank.

Many ornithologists believe that the northern mocking birds are __________ wild birds in the jungle.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. the noisiest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Describing the mocking birds as the loudest among all the wild birds in the jungle requires the superlative degree with the definite article "the" — "the noisiest wild birds".

◦ Correct: ... the northern mocking birds are the noisiest wild birds in the jungle.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "the noisy" (positive with wrong article) and Option 2 "noisy" (positive) lack the superlative sense.

• Option 4 "noisier" is the comparative (used with "than").

NOTE

• Degrees of "noisy" (a "-y" adjective): noisy – noisier – noisiest. The superlative takes "the" and compares three or more; "in the jungle" (a whole group) signals the superlative.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.

The rivals in the institution _____ (fabricated) evidence and manipulated the whole dataset.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. forged.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fabricated" means invented or made up (something false); forged. Its closest synonym is "forged", meaning to produce a fake/false copy or invent falsely. (गढ़ा हुआ / जाली बनाना)

◦ Example: They fabricated/forged documents to cheat the bank.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "destroyed" (ruined), Option 3 "fluctuated" (varied) and Option 4 "wrecked" (badly damaged) do not mean "invented falsely".

NOTE

• Synonyms of fabricate: forge, falsify, concoct, invent, make up.

• "Fabricate" has two senses: (1) to construct/manufacture, and (2) to invent something false. Here the second sense applies.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error in phrasal verb.

Tina dropped behind of / college and / went straight / into a good job.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Tina dropped behind of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct phrasal verb is "drop out of" (to leave school/college before finishing), not "drop behind of". "Drop behind" means to fall behind others, which does not fit here.

◦ Correct: Tina dropped out of college and went straight into a good job.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "college and", "went straight" and "into a good job" are all correct.

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "drop": drop out (of) = quit (school); drop in/by = visit briefly; drop off = leave someone/fall asleep; drop behind = fall behind. Note the preposition "of" in "drop out of college".

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Endengered.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Endengered" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Endangered", meaning put at risk or in danger (e.g., a species threatened with extinction). (संकटग्रस्त / खतरे में)

◦ Example: The tiger is an endangered species.

• Spelling key: EN + DANGER + ED — it contains the word "danger".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Spouse" (husband/wife), "Intransigence" (refusal to change one's views) and "Unambiguous" (clear) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related word: endanger (verb). Remember it is built from "danger" — endanger, endangered, endangerment.

question: Identify the ODD word from the given options.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Golf.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Golf" is the odd one out because it is an outdoor sport, played on a large open course, whereas Billiards, Table tennis and Carom are typically indoor games played on a table. (गोल्फ — बाहरी खेल)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Golf is played by hitting a ball into a series of holes using clubs, on a large outdoor course.

• Billiards, table tennis (ping-pong) and carrom are all table/indoor games.

NOTE

• In "odd one out" questions, look for the common feature shared by three options; the one lacking it is the answer. Here the common feature is "indoor table game".

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

My friend, / Priya looks more cheerful today / as she celebrates her birthday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. No error.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "My friend, Priya looks more cheerful today as she celebrates her birthday" is grammatically correct. The comparative "more cheerful" is fine (comparing her mood today with usual), "as" means "because", and the appositive "My friend, Priya" is correctly punctuated.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 (No error).

Additional Information

• "My friend," is a correct appositive introducing Priya.

• "more cheerful today" and "as she celebrates her birthday" are both grammatically sound.

NOTE

• In "spot the error" questions, if all segments are correct, choose "No error". Do not assume there must always be a mistake.

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

Arun asks Smita to copy the contents of the document word by word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. word for word.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct idiomatic phrase is "word for word", meaning exactly, in precisely the same words. Hence "copy the contents ... word for word". (शब्दशः / हूबहू)

◦ Example: She repeated his statement word for word.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "word par word", "word with word" and "word to word" are not standard English expressions.

NOTE

• Similar fixed phrases: "face to face", "side by side", "step by step", "back to back", "day by day". "Word for word" = verbatim.

question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

The new almirah is big than this one.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. bigger.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" requires the comparative degree. The comparative of the short adjective "big" is "bigger" (double the "g" and add "-er").

◦ Correct: The new almirah is bigger than this one.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "more big" and Option 4 "more bigger" are wrong (short adjectives don't take "more"; "more bigger" is a double comparative).

• Option 3 "biggest" is the superlative, used with "the", not "than".

NOTE

• Consonant-doubling rule: short vowel + single consonant → double it before "-er/-est": big → bigger → biggest; hot → hotter; thin → thinner.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM to substitute the underlined word in the given sentence.

In what ways do you find technological advancements beneficial to your daily life?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. unfavourable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Beneficial" means helpful, favourable or advantageous. Its antonym is "unfavourable", meaning not helpful, harmful or disadvantageous. (लाभकारी का विलोम — प्रतिकूल)

◦ Example: The new policy was beneficial for farmers but unfavourable for traders.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "unfathomable" (impossible to understand), Option 3 "unapproachable" (unfriendly/inaccessible) and Option 4 "unwarranted" (unjustified) are not antonyms of "beneficial".

NOTE

• Synonyms of beneficial: advantageous, favourable, helpful, useful, profitable.

• Antonyms: unfavourable, harmful, detrimental, disadvantageous.

question:
Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank.

We are entering a point where technology will change at __________ speeds.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. extreme.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Extreme" is the correctly spelt word, meaning very great in degree; reaching the highest or furthest point. (अत्यधिक / चरम)

◦ Example: The climbers faced extreme cold on the summit.

• Spelling key: EX + TREME — ends in "-treme".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "inferier" (correct: inferior), Option 3 "suprime" (correct: supreme) and Option 4 "modarate" (correct: moderate) are all misspellings.

NOTE

• Related forms: extreme, extremely, extremity, extremist. Watch the "-eme" ending in extreme, supreme, scheme, theme.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Leisure activities can improve an individual's physical and mental health by _______ stress, and offering a pleasurable experience.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. relieving.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Relieving" means reducing or removing (pain, stress or difficulty). Leisure activities improve health by relieving (reducing) stress. (तनाव कम करना)

◦ Example: A short walk is good for relieving stress.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "irritating" and Option 4 "upsetting" have a negative sense (increasing stress), contradicting the positive tone.

• Option 1 "reconstructing" (rebuilding) does not collocate with "stress".

NOTE

• Collocations with "relieve": relieve stress/pain/pressure/tension/anxiety. Synonyms: ease, alleviate, reduce, lessen, soothe.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Entice
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Repulse.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Entice" means to attract or tempt someone by offering something desirable. Its antonym is "repulse", meaning to drive away or cause a feeling of disgust. (लुभाना का विलोम — विकर्षित करना)

◦ Example: The advertisement tried to entice buyers, but the smell repulsed them.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Allure" and Option 3 "Invite" are synonyms (or near-synonyms) of entice.

• Option 4 "Tangle" (to twist/knot) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of entice: tempt, lure, allure, attract, coax.

• Antonyms: repulse, repel, deter, disgust, put off.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

School classrooms have __________ very little over the last century.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. changed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Changed" (past participle of "change") fits the present perfect tense ("have changed") and the phrase "over the last century", meaning classrooms have altered very little over a long period up to now. (बदला है)

◦ Correct: School classrooms have changed very little over the last century.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "freed" (released) and Option 3 "startled" (surprised) do not suit "very little over the last century".

• Option 4 "unconcerned" is an adjective and cannot follow "have" to make sense here.

NOTE

• Present perfect (has/have + V3) with "over the last century / for years / since" shows a change or state continuing up to the present. "Change very little" = alter only slightly.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Dolphins 1_____ regarded as the friendliest creatures in the sea, and stories of them helping drowning sailors have been common since Roman times. The more we 2_____ about dolphins, the more we realise that their society is more complex 3_____ people previously imagined. They look 4_____ other dolphins when they are ill, care for pregnant 5_____ and protect the weakest in the community, as we do.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. are.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "Dolphins" is plural, and the statement is a general present truth in the passive ("are regarded as"), so the plural verb "are" is correct.

◦ Correct: Dolphins are regarded as the friendliest creatures in the sea.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "has" and Option 4 "is" are singular and do not agree with the plural "Dolphins".

• Option 2 "was" is past singular and breaks the present-tense general statement.

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement: a plural subject (dolphins) takes a plural verb (are). "Be regarded as" is a passive structure meaning "to be considered as".

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Dolphins 1_____ regarded as the friendliest creatures in the sea, and stories of them helping drowning sailors have been common since Roman times. The more we 2_____ about dolphins, the more we realise that their society is more complex 3_____ people previously imagined. They look 4_____ other dolphins when they are ill, care for pregnant 5_____ and protect the weakest in the community, as we do.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. learn.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "we" takes the base form of the verb in the simple present. In the "The more ... the more ..." structure, the verb stays in the present tense — "The more we learn about dolphins ...".

◦ Correct: The more we learn about dolphins, the more we realise ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "learns" is for third person singular (he/she/it), not "we".

• Option 2 "learning" (-ing) and Option 3 "learned" (past) do not fit the present-tense parallel structure.

NOTE

• The "The + comparative ... , the + comparative ..." pattern shows that two things increase together: "The more you practise, the better you become".

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Dolphins 1_____ regarded as the friendliest creatures in the sea, and stories of them helping drowning sailors have been common since Roman times. The more we 2_____ about dolphins, the more we realise that their society is more complex 3_____ people previously imagined. They look 4_____ other dolphins when they are ill, care for pregnant 5_____ and protect the weakest in the community, as we do.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. than.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The comparative adjective "more complex" must be followed by "than" to complete the comparison — "more complex than people previously imagined". (की तुलना में)

◦ Correct: ... their society is more complex than people previously imagined.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "for", 2 "the" and 4 "to" cannot follow a comparative adjective in this structure.

NOTE

• Comparative degree is always paired with "than": bigger than, more complex than, better than. Do not confuse "than" (comparison) with "then" (time).

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Dolphins 1_____ regarded as the friendliest creatures in the sea, and stories of them helping drowning sailors have been common since Roman times. The more we 2_____ about dolphins, the more we realise that their society is more complex 3_____ people previously imagined. They look 4_____ other dolphins when they are ill, care for pregnant 5_____ and protect the weakest in the community, as we do.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. after.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "look after" means to take care of someone. Dolphins "look after other dolphins when they are ill" — i.e., they care for the sick ones. (देखभाल करना)

◦ Correct: They look after other dolphins when they are ill.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "look up" (search for information / improve), "look on" (to watch without taking part) and "look into" (to investigate) do not fit the sense of caring.

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "look": look after (care for), look for (search), look into (investigate), look up (search a reference), look up to (admire), look down on (despise).

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Dolphins 1_____ regarded as the friendliest creatures in the sea, and stories of them helping drowning sailors have been common since Roman times. The more we 2_____ about dolphins, the more we realise that their society is more complex 3_____ people previously imagined. They look 4_____ other dolphins when they are ill, care for pregnant 5_____ and protect the weakest in the community, as we do.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. mothers.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Only females (mothers) can be pregnant, so the phrase "care for pregnant mothers" is the only logical and grammatically correct choice. (गर्भवती माताएँ)

◦ Correct: ... care for pregnant mothers and protect the weakest ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "brothers", 3 "fathers" and 4 "uncles" refer to males, who cannot be "pregnant", so they are incorrect.

NOTE

• Read the whole sentence for context; the adjective "pregnant" restricts the noun to a female (mother), making the answer clear.

question: Which of the following states had benefitted by the Indira Gandhi Canal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indira Gandhi Canal (formerly the Rajasthan Canal) is the longest canal in India and has greatly benefitted the arid state of Rajasthan by bringing irrigation and drinking water to the Thar Desert region. (इंदिरा गांधी नहर — राजस्थान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The canal takes off from the Harike Barrage (at the confluence of the Sutlej and Beas rivers) in Punjab.

• It has transformed desert districts like Bikaner, Jaisalmer, Barmer and Sri Ganganagar into agriculturally productive areas.

NOTE

• Major canals/projects for SSC: Indira Gandhi Canal (Rajasthan), Bhakra-Nangal (Sutlej), Nagarjuna Sagar (Krishna), Hirakud (Mahanadi).

question: Which of the following is the style of temple architecture that is widely favoured in northern India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nagar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Nagara" style of temple architecture is the style widely favoured in northern India. Its most distinctive feature is the curvilinear (beehive-shaped) tower called the "Shikhara" over the sanctum (garbhagriha). (नागर शैली — उत्तर भारत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The "Dravida" style (South India) has a pyramidal tower called the "Vimana" and a gateway tower called the "Gopuram".

• The "Vesara" style is a hybrid of Nagara and Dravida, seen in the Deccan (e.g., Hoysala temples).

NOTE

• Examples of Nagara temples: Kandariya Mahadeva (Khajuraho), Sun Temple (Konark), Lingaraja (Bhubaneswar). Examples of Dravida: Brihadeeswara Temple (Thanjavur), Meenakshi Temple (Madurai).

question: 'My Country My Life' is the autobiography of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lal Krishna Advani.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "My Country My Life" (2008) is the autobiography of the veteran BJP leader Lal Krishna Advani. (माई कंट्री माई लाइफ — लालकृष्ण आडवाणी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• L. K. Advani served as the Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of India and was a key figure in Indian politics. He was awarded the Bharat Ratna (announced 2024).

NOTE

• Famous political autobiographies: "A Prime Minister to Remember" (P. C. Alexander), "One Life is Not Enough" (Natwar Singh), "The Turbulent Years / The Coalition Years" (Pranab Mukherjee), "Truth, Love & A Little Malice" (Khushwant Singh).

question: In which of the following systems was the charge of collecting the revenue and paying it to the Company given to the village headman, rather than the zamindar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahalwari.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Mahalwari system, land revenue was assessed on a whole village or estate ("mahal"), and the responsibility of collecting the revenue and paying it to the Company was given to the village headman (lambardar) / village community, rather than to a zamindar. (महलवारी व्यवस्था)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Mahalwari system was introduced by Holt Mackenzie (1822) and later modified by William Bentinck; it was applied in parts of North-Western Provinces, Central India and Punjab.

• In the Zamindari (Permanent Settlement, 1793) system of Lord Cornwallis, zamindars collected revenue.

• In the Ryotwari system (introduced by Thomas Munro and Alexander Read), revenue was collected directly from individual cultivators (ryots).

NOTE

• The three main British land revenue systems: Permanent/Zamindari (Bengal), Ryotwari (Madras & Bombay), Mahalwari (North-West & Central).

question: Who among the following signed a pact with Lord Irwin on March 5, 1931?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Gandhi–Irwin Pact was signed on 5 March 1931 between Mahatma Gandhi and Lord Irwin (the then Viceroy of India). (गांधी-इरविन समझौता)

• As per the pact, Gandhi agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement and participate in the Second Round Table Conference, and the government agreed to release political prisoners.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The pact is also called the Delhi Pact.

• It allowed people living near the coast to make salt for personal use.

NOTE

• Related events: Civil Disobedience Movement (1930, Dandi March), Round Table Conferences (1930–32), Poona Pact (1932, between Gandhi and Ambedkar).

question: A river is capable of forming which of the following landscapes when the river is in its middle course?
solution_text:
The correct answer is A meander.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In its middle course, a river flows over gentler slopes and, through erosion on the outer bank and deposition on the inner bank, develops large bends called "meanders". (मध्य मार्ग — विसर्प / मीएंडर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Upper course (youthful stage) landforms: V-shaped valleys, waterfalls, gorges, rapids (mostly erosional).

• Middle course (mature stage) landforms: meanders, ox-bow lakes, alluvial fans.

• Lower course (old stage) landforms: floodplains, levees, deltas, distributaries (mostly depositional).

NOTE

• A cut-off meander loop forms an "ox-bow lake". Deltas (e.g., the Sundarbans) form at the river's mouth in the lower course.

question: Which of the following mountain peaks is a part of the Himalayas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kamet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kamet" (7,756 m) is a high peak of the Himalayas, located in the Garhwal region of Uttarakhand, near the Tibet border. It is the second-highest peak in the Garhwal Himalayas after Nanda Devi. (कामेट — हिमालय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Dhupgarh" is the highest peak of the Satpura Range (Madhya Pradesh).

• "Kalsubai" is the highest peak in Maharashtra (Western Ghats/Sahyadri).

• "Taramati" is a peak in the Nilgiri/Deccan region.

NOTE

• Highest peaks: Mount Everest (world), Kangchenjunga (highest in India), K2/Godwin-Austen (highest in the Indian subcontinent, in PoK).

question: Which of the following is NOT related to goals of Fundamental Duties of Indian Citizens?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Courage.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Among the given words, "Courage" is NOT directly listed as a goal/keyword in the Fundamental Duties (Article 51A). The duties speak of citizens being asked to cherish noble ideals, respect the Constitution/National Flag/Anthem, and preserve the rich heritage and environment — but not "courage". (साहस — मौलिक कर्तव्यों में नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Fundamental Duties (Part IV-A, Article 51A) include: to abide by the Constitution, cherish the ideals of the freedom struggle, protect the sovereignty and integrity of India, respect the National Flag and Anthem, preserve the rich heritage and environment, develop scientific temper, etc.

• They were added by the 42nd Amendment (1976) on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

NOTE

• There are 11 Fundamental Duties (the 11th, on education of children, was added by the 86th Amendment, 2002). They are non-justiciable.

question: Which team won the Women's Asian Hockey Champions Trophy in 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indian women's hockey team won the Women's Asian Champions Trophy 2023, held at Ranchi, Jharkhand, defeating Japan in the final. (महिला एशियाई चैंपियंस ट्रॉफी 2023 — भारत)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Asian Champions Trophy is an international field hockey tournament among the top Asian teams, organised by the Asian Hockey Federation.

• India has been a strong performer in both the men's and women's editions.

NOTE

• Hockey is closely associated with India; Major Dhyan Chand (the "Hockey Wizard") led India to Olympic golds, and 29 August (his birthday) is National Sports Day.

question: S Abdul Nazeer was appointed as the Governor of __________ in February 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Justice S. Abdul Nazeer, a former Judge of the Supreme Court of India, was appointed the Governor of Andhra Pradesh in February 2023. (एस. अब्दुल नज़ीर — आंध्र प्रदेश के राज्यपाल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• A Governor is the constitutional head of a state, appointed by the President under Article 155, and holds office during the pleasure of the President (Article 156).

• The Governor must be a citizen of India and at least 35 years of age.

NOTE

• Justice S. Abdul Nazeer was part of the Supreme Court benches in landmark cases such as the Ayodhya verdict (2019) and the Triple Talaq case (2017).

question: Which Tamil superstar founded the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) political party in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry on 2 February 2024 with the slogan 'Pirappokkum Ellaa Uyirkkum' (All are equal by birth)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vijay.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Tamil superstar Vijay (Thalapathy Vijay) founded the political party Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) on 2 February 2024, with the slogan "Pirappokkum Ellaa Uyirkkum" ("All are equal by birth"), a line from the Tamil poet Bharathiyar. (विजय — तमिलागा वेट्री कषगम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The slogan reflects the party's emphasis on social equality and justice.

• Tamil Nadu has a long tradition of film stars entering politics (e.g., MGR, Jayalalithaa, Karunanidhi).

NOTE

• "Kazhagam" means "association/federation" in Tamil (as in DMK — Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam, AIADMK).

question: The digestive enzymes inside lysosomes are made by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is rough endoplasmic reticulum.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The digestive (hydrolytic) enzymes present inside lysosomes are proteins, and all proteins in the cell are synthesised by the ribosomes on the rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER). (लाइसोसोम के एंजाइम — रफ एंडोप्लाज्मिक रेटिकुलम)

• After being made by the RER, the enzymes are packaged by the Golgi apparatus into lysosomes.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Lysosomes are known as the "suicidal bags of the cell" because their enzymes can digest worn-out cell parts and even the cell itself.

• The Golgi apparatus modifies and packages the enzymes but does not synthesise them.

NOTE

• The Rough ER (studded with ribosomes) makes proteins; the Smooth ER makes lipids. Ribosomes are the actual "protein factories" of the cell.

question: __________ was well known for creating fusion art by adapting European theatrical techniques to Indian classical dance combined with Indian folk and tribal dance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uday Shankar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Uday Shankar was a pioneering dancer and choreographer well known for creating a fusion style by blending European theatrical techniques with Indian classical, folk and tribal dance. (उदय शंकर — फ्यूज़न नृत्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• He popularised Indian dance in the West and was awarded the Padma Vibhushan.

• He was the elder brother of the famous sitar maestro Pandit Ravi Shankar.

NOTE

• Guru Bipin Singh — Manipuri; Kelucharan Mohapatra — Odissi; Birju Maharaj — Kathak (Lucknow gharana). Uday Shankar is remembered specifically for fusion/creative dance.

question: What is the primary gas responsible for the leavening effect in bread when yeast ferments sugars?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Carbon dioxide.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When yeast ferments the sugars in dough, it produces carbon dioxide (CO₂) gas (and ethanol). The CO₂ gets trapped in the dough, forming bubbles that make the bread rise and become soft and spongy — this is the leavening effect. (किण्वन — कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The process is anaerobic respiration (fermentation): Sugar → Ethanol + Carbon dioxide + Energy.

• The same fermentation is used in making idli, dosa batter and alcoholic beverages.

NOTE

• Baking soda (sodium bicarbonate) also releases CO₂ on heating, giving a similar leavening effect in cakes and other baked goods.

question: Who was the famous Venetian traveller of the 13th century who visited Kerala?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Marco Polo.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Marco Polo was the famous Venetian (Italian) traveller of the 13th century who visited Kerala (and other parts of India) around 1288–1293 on his way back from China. (मार्को पोलो — 13वीं शताब्दी)

• He recorded his travels in his book "Il Milione (The Travels of Marco Polo)".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Abdur Razzaq — Persian traveller who visited the Vijayanagara Empire (15th century).

• Nicolo Conti — Italian traveller who also visited Vijayanagara.

• Ludovico di Varthema (Barthema) — early 16th-century Italian traveller.

NOTE

• Foreign travellers to India for SSC: Fa-Hien (5th c.), Hiuen Tsang / Xuanzang (7th c.), Al-Biruni (11th c.), Ibn Battuta (14th c., Moroccan).

question: What is Cash Reserve Ratio?
option_1: Percentage of deposits that a central bank must keep as cash reserves with the bank
option_2: Percentage of deposits that a central bank must keep as cash reserves with the government
option_3: Percentage of deposits that a bank must keep as cash reserves with any bank
option_4: Percentage of deposits that a bank must keep as cash reserves with the central bank
solution_text:
The correct answer is Percentage of deposits that a bank must keep as cash reserves with the central bank.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is the percentage of a commercial bank's total deposits that it must keep as cash reserves with the central bank (the RBI in India). (नकद आरक्षित अनुपात — सीआरआर)

• Banks earn no interest on the amount kept as CRR.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The RBI uses CRR as a tool of monetary policy: raising the CRR reduces the money available for lending (controls inflation), while lowering it increases liquidity.

• The Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) is the percentage of deposits a bank must keep in liquid assets (cash, gold, government securities) with itself.

NOTE

• Key RBI monetary policy rates: Repo rate, Reverse repo rate, CRR, SLR, Bank rate, MSF. CRR and SLR are quantitative tools that control credit and liquidity.

question: Sarhul is an agricultural festival of tribals, which is primarily celebrated in the Indian state of __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jharkhand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sarhul" is a spring/agricultural festival of the tribal communities (such as the Oraon, Munda and Ho tribes), primarily celebrated in Jharkhand (and neighbouring tribal regions). It marks the worship of nature, especially the Sal tree, at the beginning of the new year. (सरहुल — झारखंड)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• During Sarhul, the village priest (Pahan) worships the village deity, and Sal flowers are offered.

• Other tribal festivals of Jharkhand: Karma, Tusu and Sohrai.

NOTE

• Sarhul reflects the deep bond between tribal communities and nature; "Sarhul" means the worship of the Sal tree.

question: According to Census 2011, what is the sex ratio of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 943.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census 2011, the sex ratio of India was 943, meaning there were 943 females per 1,000 males. (लिंगानुपात — 943)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The sex ratio improved from 933 (2001) to 943 (2011).

• Kerala had the highest sex ratio (1,084), and Haryana the lowest (879) among the states.

• The child sex ratio (0–6 years) in 2011 was 919, a matter of concern, addressed by schemes like "Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao".

NOTE

• Sex ratio = (number of females ÷ number of males) × 1000. It is an important indicator of gender equality and social health.

question: Kalamandalam Krishnan Nair was a notable figure in which of the following classical dance forms of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathakali.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kalamandalam Krishnan Nair was a legendary exponent of the Kathakali classical dance-drama of Kerala, renowned for his powerful expression (abhinaya). (कथकली — कलामंडलम कृष्णन नायर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kathakali is famous for its elaborate costumes, towering headgear, vivid green ("Pacha") make-up and stories from the Ramayana and Mahabharata.

• "Kalamandalam" is the prefix used by artists trained at the famous Kerala Kalamandalam institution founded by the poet Vallathol Narayana Menon.

NOTE

• Classical dances of Kerala: Kathakali and Mohiniyattam. Both are traditionally accompanied by Carnatic/Sopana music.

question: Who was the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India for the 2011 Indian Census?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dr. C Chandramouli.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dr. C. Chandramouli was the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India for the 2011 Census (the 15th national census of India). (2011 जनगणना आयुक्त — डॉ. सी. चंद्रमौली)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India (ORGI) works under the Ministry of Home Affairs and is responsible for the decennial Census and civil registration.

• The Census 2011 theme was "Our Census, Our Future".

NOTE

• The first census in India was conducted in 1872 (under Lord Mayo) and the first synchronous/complete census in 1881 (under Lord Ripon). The census is held every 10 years.

question: Helium gas can be converted to the liquid form by the __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is London forces of attraction.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Helium is a non-polar, monatomic noble gas, so it has no permanent dipole. It can be liquefied only because of the very weak, temporary "London dispersion forces" (a type of van der Waals force) that arise from instantaneous dipoles due to the momentary movement of electrons. (लंदन बल — हीलियम का द्रवीकरण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Hydrogen bonding (option 1) occurs in molecules like water, HF and NH₃ — not in helium.

• Dipole–dipole and dipole–induced dipole forces require a permanent dipole, which helium lacks.

• Helium has the lowest boiling point of all elements (about 4 K / −269 °C).

NOTE

• Van der Waals forces (in increasing strength): London dispersion < dipole–dipole < hydrogen bonding. Even the weak London forces are enough to liquefy helium at extremely low temperatures.

question: The sister of Harshavardhana Rajyashri was married to __________, the king of Maukhari dynasty of Kanyakubja.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Grahavarman.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rajyashri, the sister of Harshavardhana, was married to Grahavarman, the king of the Maukhari dynasty of Kanyakubja (Kannauj). (राज्यश्री का विवाह ग्रहवर्मन से)

• Grahavarman was later killed by Devagupta (the king of Malwa), an event that drew Harsha into war and eventually led to his rise.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Harshavardhana (r. 606–647 CE) of the Pushyabhuti (Vardhana) dynasty ruled from Thanesar and later Kannauj.

• The Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang) visited India during Harsha's reign. Harsha's court poet Banabhatta wrote the "Harshacharita".

NOTE

• Harsha was defeated by the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II on the banks of the Narmada, which checked his expansion to the south.

question: Pandit Arvind Thatte belongs to which of the following gharanas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mewati gharana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Arvind Thatte, a Hindustani classical vocalist, belongs to the Mewati gharana of Indian classical music. (मेवाती घराना — पंडित अरविंद थत्ते)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Mewati gharana is best known through Pandit Jasraj, one of its greatest exponents.

• A "gharana" is a system of social organisation/lineage linking musicians or dancers by a particular musical style.

NOTE

• Major Hindustani vocal gharanas: Gwalior (oldest), Agra, Kirana, Jaipur-Atrauli, Patiala, Mewati and Banaras.

question: In the inaugural year of the Nehru Cup event for football in 1982, which team emerged as the winner of the first edition?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uruguay.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first edition of the Nehru Cup football tournament, held in 1982, was won by Uruguay. (नेहरू कप 1982 — उरुग्वे विजेता)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Nehru Cup was an international football tournament organised by the All India Football Federation (AIFF) in memory of Jawaharlal Nehru.

• The Indian national football team won the Nehru Cup three times (2007, 2009 and 2012).

NOTE

• India's football icon Sunil Chhetri played key roles in India's Nehru Cup victories. The AIFF is the governing body for football in India.

question: Who among the following is the ex-officio Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha as on 10 October 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jagdeep Dhankar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairperson (Chairman) of the Rajya Sabha. As on 10 October 2023, the Vice-President was Jagdeep Dhankhar, who therefore chaired the Rajya Sabha. (राज्यसभा के पदेन सभापति — जगदीप धनखड़)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Under Article 64 and Article 89, the Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

• The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Harivansh Narayan Singh at the time) is elected from among its members.

NOTE

• The Lok Sabha is presided over by the Speaker (elected from among its members). The Vice-President does not preside over the Lok Sabha.
